_what: Romanized Hebrew words that Google Input Tools mis-hears, and the Hebrew the learner means. Applied by quicksay.js before the phonetic query: the word is replaced by its Hebrew, which Input Tools passes through untouched, so it only has to guess the words we do not already know.
_how_measured: tools/romanization-probe.mjs — every row's romanization is typed as a learner would (lowercased, syllable hyphens removed) and Input Tools' first answer is compared word by word to the verified Hebrew, raw and through the page's own phoneticQuery. Every entry below was WRONG in that measurement. Keys may be written in any spelling: the page folds them (lowercase, kh->ch, tz->ts, letters only) at load, so achshav and akhshav are one key.
_rule_for_adding: Only a word whose romanization has ONE plausible Hebrew reading. lo (לא/לו), im (עם/אם), ken (כן), ma-im — anything a learner could mean two ways stays OUT, because a wrong fix here is worse than Input Tools' wrong guess: it is our confident wrong guess. Spelling variants (בעייה/בעיה, השירותים/השרותים) are not errors and are not here.
_provenance: Entries up to 'tedaber' were mined from data/phrasebook.json on 2026-08-17, so the phrasebook score in romanization-probe.mjs is IN-SAMPLE for them. 'cham' exists because the word-initial ch->h rule in quicksay.js turns it into הם — the fix list is consulted before that rule. 'ata', 'od', 'dai' were seen wrong on the expressions set on 2026-08-18, which makes the expressions score in-sample for those three words only; every other expressions row remains held-out.
